text: 3M’s capital expenditures rose from $1.373 billion in fiscal 2017 to $1.577 billion in fiscal 2018, an increase of $204 million[1][4]. The company said it invests in renewal and maintenance programs that reduce costs, improve cycle time, maintain and renew current capacity, eliminate pollution, and ensure compliance[2]. It also invests in growth by adding capacity through expansion of existing facilities and construction of new facilities driven by new products[2]. Additional investments include information technology and laboratory facilities[2]. In 2018, 63% of capital spending was in the United States as 3M increased investment in manufacturing and sourcing capability to better align product capability with sales in major geographic areas[3].

sql:
WITH cap AS (
    SELECT fiscal_year, value
    FROM annual_values
    WHERE cik = (SELECT cik FROM companies WHERE name = '3M')
      AND metric = 'capital_expenditure'
      AND fiscal_year IN (2017, 2018)
)
SELECT 
    MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2017 THEN value END) AS cap_2017,
    MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2018 THEN value END) AS cap_2018,
    ROUND(
        MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2018 THEN value END) -
        MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2017 THEN value END), 2
    ) AS change
FROM cap

text: Net income attributable to shareholders fell from $6,527 million in 2016 to $1,248 million in 2017, a decline of $5,279 million[1][2]. The decline was driven by a 15% drop in net operating revenues, which fell to $35,410 million from $41,863 million[2]. Other operating charges increased 43% to $2,157 million from $1,510 million, adding pressure on earnings[2]. Income taxes from continuing operations surged to $5,560 million in 2017, raising the effective tax rate to 82.5% from 19.5% in 2016, which sharply reduced net income[2]. Together, lower revenues, higher operating charges, and a much higher tax expense explain the sharp fall in net income[2].

sql:
SELECT 
    ROUND(av2016.value, 2) AS net_income_2016,
    ROUND(av2017.value, 2) AS net_income_2017,
    ROUND(av2016.value - av2017.value, 2) AS fall_amount
FROM annual_values AS av2016
JOIN annual_values AS av2017
  ON av2016.cik = av2017.cik
 AND av2016.metric = av2017.metric
 AND av2016.fiscal_year = 2016
 AND av2017.fiscal_year = 2017
JOIN companies AS c
  ON c.cik = av2016.cik
WHERE c.name = 'Coca-Cola'
  AND av2016.metric = 'net_income'
  AND av2017.metric = 'net_income'

text: Walmart's consolidated operating income increased from $20.437 billion in fiscal 2018 to $21.957 billion in fiscal 2019, a rise of $1.520 billion [1][5]. The 2019 Form 10‑K notes that segment operating income grew $391 million in fiscal 2019, driven by strong sales performance and productivity improvements that more than offset investments in eCommerce, technology, omni‑channel initiatives and higher wages [2][3]. It also attributes the increase to pricing strategy effects, transportation expense changes, and mix impacts from the expanding eCommerce business, while operating expenses as a percentage of sales fell, further supporting income growth [3]. The International segment contributed to the rise with net sales growth from the Flipkart acquisition and positive comparable sales, partially offset by divestitures and currency impacts [2].

text: Nike's revenues increased by $2.72 billion, from $36.397 billion in fiscal 2018 to $39.117 billion in fiscal 2019, a 7.47% increase [1][8]. The growth was driven by strong NIKE Direct performance, with digital commerce sales rising sharply (28%‑35% growth) and comparable store sales up about 10%‑14%, as well as higher footwear and apparel sales led by Sportswear and higher average selling prices, and contributions from all geographic regions such as Greater China, North America and EMEA each adding roughly 3 percentage points of growth [2][3][4][7].

sql:
WITH nike_data AS (
    SELECT
        av.fiscal_year,
        av.metric,
        av.value
    FROM annual_values av
    JOIN companies c ON av.cik = c.cik
    WHERE c.name = 'Nike'
      AND av.fiscal_year IN (2018, 2019)
      AND av.metric IN ('revenue', 'gross_profit', 'operating_income', 'net_income')
)
SELECT
    MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2018 AND metric = 'revenue'        THEN value END) AS revenue_2018,
    MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2019 AND metric = 'revenue'        THEN value END) AS revenue_2019,
    ROUND(
        MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2019 AND metric = 'revenue' THEN value END) -
        MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2018 AND metric = 'revenue' THEN value END),
        2) AS revenue_growth,
    ROUND(
        100.0 *
        (MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2019 AND metric = 'revenue' THEN value END) -
         MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2018 AND metric = 'revenue' THEN value END)) /
        MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2018 AND metric = 'revenue' THEN value END),
        2) AS revenue_growth_pct,
    MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2018 AND metric = 'gross_profit'        THEN value END) AS gross_profit_2018,
    MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2019 AND metric = 'gross_profit'        THEN value END) AS gross_profit_2019,
    MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2018 AND metric = 'operating_income'   THEN value END) AS operating_income_2018,
    MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2019 AND metric = 'operating_income'   THEN value END) AS operating_income_2019,
    MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2018 AND metric = 'net_income'         THEN value END) AS net_income_2018,
    MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 2019 AND metric = 'net_income'         THEN value END) AS net_income_2019
FROM nike_data

text: MGM Resorts' revenue fell by $7.74 billion in 2020 compared with 2019, with 2020 revenue of $5.162 billion versus $12.900 billion in 2019 [1][2]. This represents a roughly 60% decline year‑over‑year [4]. The decline was caused primarily by the COVID‑19 pandemic, which led to temporary closures of domestic and regional properties, mid‑week hotel shutdowns after re‑opening, travel restrictions to Macau, suspension of the IVS, and limits on table‑game, slot‑machine and venue capacities [4].

SELECT 
    ROUND(av2019.value, 2) AS revenue_2019,
    ROUND(av2020.value, 2) AS revenue_2020,

FROM annual_values AS av2019
JOIN annual_values AS av2020

text: Boeing's total revenue rose from $93.392 billion in 2017 to $101.127 billion in 2018, an increase of $7.735 billion (≈8.3%) [1]. The company’s 10‑K also reports total revenue of $94.005 billion in 2017 and $101.127 billion in 2018, a rise of $7.122 billion (≈8%) [6][2]. The increase was driven primarily by higher segment revenues: Commercial Airplanes (BCA) grew by $2.701 billion, Defense, Space & Security (BDS) by $2.634 billion, and Global Services (BGS) by $2.437 billion [6]. These gains were partially offset by a decline in unallocated items, eliminations and other of $617 million (from $542 million in 2017 to –$75 million in 2018) [2][6]. Overall, the combined segment growth of roughly $7.8 billion explains the total revenue increase between the two years [6][2].

sql:
WITH boeing AS (
  SELECT 
    av.fiscal_year,
    MAX(CASE WHEN av.metric = 'revenue' THEN av.value END)               AS revenue,
    MAX(CASE WHEN av.metric = 'gross_profit' THEN av.value END)          AS gross_profit,
    MAX(CASE WHEN av.metric = 'operating_income' THEN av.value END)      AS operating_income,
    MAX(CASE WHEN av.metric = 'net_income' THEN av.value END)            AS net_income
  FROM annual_values av
  JOIN companies c ON av.cik = c.cik
  WHERE c.name = 'Boeing'
    AND av.fiscal_year IN (2017, 2018)
  GROUP BY av.fiscal_year
)
SELECT
  a.fiscal_year                         AS year_2017,
  ROUND(a.revenue, 2)                   AS revenue_2017,
  b.fiscal_year                         AS year_2018,
  ROUND(b.revenue, 2)                   AS revenue_2018,
  ROUND(b.revenue - a.revenue, 2)       AS revenue_change,
  ROUND(b.gross_profit - a.gross_profit, 2)       AS gross_profit_change,
  ROUND(b.operating_income - a.operating_income, 2) AS operating_income_change,
  ROUND(b.net_income - a.net_income, 2)           AS net_income_change
FROM boeing a
JOIN boeing b
  ON a.fiscal_year = 2017
 AND b.fiscal_year = 2018

text: Adobe's total revenue increased from $4,795.5 million in fiscal 2015 to $5,854.4 million in fiscal 2016, a growth of $1,058.9 million (22%) [1][5][2]. The company attributes the revenue growth primarily to higher subscription revenue, especially from Creative Cloud and other creative offerings that drove a $845.8 million increase in Digital Media revenue [5][4]. Growth was also supported by increased Digital Marketing revenue of $227.7 million, driven by continued adoption of Adobe Marketing Cloud and its AEM, Analytics, and Campaign products [5][4]. Additional contributions came from an extra week in the first quarter due to a 53‑week fiscal year, which modestly boosted overall revenue [1]. Overall, the shift toward subscription and hosted services, including paid Creative Cloud, Document Cloud subscriptions, and ETLAs, is cited as the main driver of the 22% revenue increase [4][5].

text: Block’s total net revenue rose from $4.7135 billion in 2019 to $9.4976 billion in 2020, an increase of $4.7841 billion, or about 101.5% [1][2]. The increase was largely driven by a surge in bitcoin revenue, which grew by $4.055 billion (from $516.5 million to $4.5715 billion), accounting for roughly 85% of the total revenue growth [2][7]. Excluding bitcoin, total net revenue still rose by $729 million (17% growth), reflecting higher subscription and services revenue (+$507.9 million) and modest gains in hardware revenue (+$7.1 million) [2][8]. Transaction‑based revenue grew modestly by $213.9 million (7% increase) due to higher payment volume and new sellers, partially offset by COVID‑19 impacts [2][8]. Overall, the combination of bitcoin price appreciation, increased active bitcoin customers, and growth in Cash App services drove the revenue jump [3][7].

sql:
WITH vals AS (
    SELECT
        av.fiscal_year,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN av.metric = 'revenue' THEN av.value END), 2)               AS revenue,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN av.metric = 'gross_profit' THEN av.value END), 2)          AS gross_profit,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN av.metric = 'operating_income' THEN av.value END), 2)      AS operating_income,
        ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN av.metric = 'net_income' THEN av.value END), 2)            AS net_income
    FROM annual_values av
    JOIN companies c ON av.cik = c.cik
    WHERE c.name = 'Block'
      AND av.fiscal_year IN (2019, 2020)
    GROUP BY av.fiscal_year
)
SELECT
    fiscal_year,
    revenue,
    ROUND(revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY fiscal_year), 2)                         AS revenue_change,
    ROUND(
        (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY fiscal_year)) * 100.0
        / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY fiscal_year), 2
    )                                                                                  AS pct_change,
    gross_profit,
    operating_income,
    net_income
FROM vals
ORDER BY fiscal_year

text: General Mills generated free cash flow of $3,215.4 million in fiscal 2020 [1]. The 10‑K states that cash from operations was driven by net cash provided by operating activities of $3,676.2 million (approximately $3.7 billion) [2][9].

sql:
WITH op AS (
    SELECT cik, fiscal_year, value
    FROM annual_values
    WHERE metric = 'operating_cash_flow' AND fiscal_year = 2020
),
cap AS (
    SELECT cik, fiscal_year, value
    FROM annual_values
    WHERE metric = 'capital_expenditure' AND fiscal_year = 2020
)
SELECT 
    c.name,
    op.fiscal_year,
    ROUND(op.value - cap.value, 2) AS free_cash_flow
FROM op
JOIN cap ON op.cik = cap.cik AND op.fiscal_year = cap.fiscal_year
JOIN companies c ON op.cik = c.cik
WHERE c.name = 'General Mills'

WITH rev AS (
    SELECT 
        av.fiscal_year,
        av.value AS revenue,
        LAG(av.value) OVER (PARTITION BY av.cik ORDER BY av.fiscal_year) AS prev_rev
    FROM annual_values av
    JOIN companies c ON av.cik = c.cik
    WHERE c.name = 'Boeing'
      AND av.metric = 'revenue'
      AND av.fiscal_year BETWEEN 2018 AND 2022
)
SELECT 
    fiscal_year,
    ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue_usd,
    ROUND(revenue - prev_rev, 2) AS yoy_change_usd
FROM rev
ORDER BY fiscal_year
